9020799b50.b: Observed on Śukla-Trayōdaśī tithi of Kārttikaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
9020799b50.d: Last three days of kārttika-māsaḥ. anantaphaladam! Perform Shiva/Vishnu Puja, Bhagavata Parayanam, BhagavadGita Parayanam, Vishnu Sahasranama Parayanam etc.
9020799b50.s:
𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌕𑍇।  
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌃 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾𑌵𑌹𑌾𑌃॥௧॥  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌿𑌣𑍀 𑌸𑌂𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌹𑌾।  
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌂 𑌯𑍋 𑌵𑍈 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌕𑌰𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌹॥௨॥  
𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌸𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇 𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌗𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍂𑌨𑍍 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌹𑌿॥௩॥  
𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌯𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾 𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍂𑌨𑍍 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌹𑌿।  
𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍁𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌨𑌾 𑌸𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌹𑌿॥௪॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌘𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌪𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍂𑌨𑍍 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌹𑌿।  
𑌉𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍋𑌦𑌕𑍇𑌨 𑌯𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇॥௫॥  
𑌰𑍌𑌰𑌵𑌂 𑌨𑌰𑌕𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶।  
𑌆𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍇𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇॥௬॥  
𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌮𑍋𑌦𑌤𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌰𑍇।  
𑌯𑍋 𑌵𑍈 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌂 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌯 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃॥௭॥  
𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑌿 𑌕𑌰𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾 𑌸 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑌰𑌕𑌂 𑌧𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌵𑌮𑍍।  
𑌕𑍁𑌟𑍁𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌭𑍋𑌜𑌨𑌂 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇॥௮॥  
𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌨𑍍𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌧𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌸 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑌂 𑌪𑌦𑌮𑍍।  
𑌗𑍀𑌤𑌾𑌪𑌾𑌠𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌯𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍇 𑌚 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇॥௯॥  
𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇𑌽𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑌮𑍇𑌤𑌿 𑌨 𑌸𑌂𑌶𑌯𑌃।  
𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌠𑌨𑌂 𑌯𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇॥௧௦॥  
𑌨 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌕𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌿𑌵𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌸𑌾।  
𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌮𑌨𑍁𑌜𑍈𑌃 𑌕𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌚॥௧௧॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌵𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌂 𑌕𑌃 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌿 𑌵𑌾 𑌭𑍁𑌵𑌿।  
𑌯𑍋 𑌵𑍈 𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌵𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌶𑍃𑌣𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌚 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌮𑍍॥௧௨॥  
𑌕𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌭𑌾𑌵𑍋 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌨𑌿𑌷𑍇𑌵𑌣𑌾𑌤𑍍।  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑌾 𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌾𑌗𑌮𑌰𑌣𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑌾॥௧௩॥  
𑌅𑌥 𑌵𑌾 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌨𑌿𑌷𑍇𑌵𑌣𑌾𑌤𑍍।  
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌯𑌃 𑌕𑌰𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇॥௧௪॥  
𑌨 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌵𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌕𑍋𑌟𑌿𑌶𑌤𑍈𑌰𑌪𑌿।  
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇॥௧௫॥  
𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌰𑌾𑌕𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌨𑌘।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑌃𑌕𑌾𑌲𑍇 𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌯 𑌶𑍌𑌚𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌚𑌰𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௧௬॥  
𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌚𑌰𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌉𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍇 𑌵𑌾 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍇 𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌰𑌃॥௧௭॥  
𑌮𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌪𑌂 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌤 𑌕𑌦𑌲𑍀𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌮𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌚𑍂𑌤𑌪𑌲𑍍𑌲𑌵𑌸𑌂𑌵𑍀𑌤𑌮𑌿𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍁𑌦𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑍁𑌮𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍॥௧௮॥  
𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌚𑍂𑌤𑌪𑌲𑍍𑌲𑌵𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌢𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌃 𑌫𑌲𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌰𑌿𑌮𑍍॥௧௯॥  
𑌶𑍃𑌣𑍁𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌮𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌨 𑌶𑍁𑌚𑌿𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍।  
𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌥 𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌥𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌵𑌾॥௨௦॥  
𑌮𑍁𑌹𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌶𑍃𑌣𑍁𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌕𑌥𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇।  
𑌯𑌦𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌤𑍁𑌮𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃॥௨௧॥  
𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇𑌽𑌥𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌿𑌥𑍌 𑌸𑌂𑌶𑍃𑌣𑍁𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌪𑌿।  
𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌵𑍇𑌨 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌰𑌃॥௨௨॥  
---𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌵𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌵𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌷𑌡𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃

903ce7c0a9.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Dvādaśī tithi of Āśvayujaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).

90b7b0e979.d: Guruḥ enters vArdhakya (old age) on 2025-May-26 21:12, 15 days before it sets into combustion (mAudhyam). At this moment guruḥ is at mr̥gaśīrṣam-3 mithunam (latitude 0°11′18.06″ S, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -1.92, elongation 21°10′15.60″ E of the Sun. A graha in vArdhakya is considered weakened, giving reduced results, though less so than in outright mAudhya.

914b9df5ac.d: Śukraḥ emerges from combustion into bAlya (infancy) on 2026-Feb-26 19:09. At this moment śukraḥ is at pūrvaprōṣṭhapadā-2 kumbhaḥ (latitude 1°23′33.40″ S, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -3.90, elongation 12°17′49.48″ E of the Sun. A graha in bAlya is likewise considered to give reduced results, for 5 days, before regaining its full strength.

9159ae4588.d: The three days around upākarma and utsarga are anadhyayana days, where one is not supposed to learn the Vedas.
9159ae4588.s:
𑌉𑌪𑌾𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌿 𑌚𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌗𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌪𑌣𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌮𑍍॥௭௫॥  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌕𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌷𑌟𑍍‌𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍇 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑍇

9164ec1b7a.b: Partial lunar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈11.0 of 12 aṅgulas), Moon at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
9164ec1b7a.d: The eclipse is already in progress at moonrise (grastodaya). Umbral magnitude: 0.91 (parimāṇa ≈11.0 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 08:54►19:53 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra maghā/pūrvaphalgunī/uttaraphalgunī (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or pūrvāṣāḍhā (anujanma) or apabharaṇī (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ get more ashubha phala, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, mēṣaḥ, karkaṭaḥ somewhat ashubha, tulā, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

91d12f6609.b: Observed on Kr̥ttikā nakshatra of Tulā (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
91d12f6609.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

Idangazhi Nayanmar, the king of Velas in Kodumbalur, was a devoted follower of Bhagavan Shiva. He ensured that all the Shiva temples in his region performed rituals as prescribed in the Shiva Agamas. In his domain, there was another devotee of Bhagavan Shiva who, due to financial difficulties, could no longer continue his practice of Maaheshwara Puja and the feeding of other devotees. Driven by his devotion and the need to continue his service, this devotee resorted to stealing paddy from Idangazhi Nayanmar's granary one night, only to be caught by the guards and brought before the king.

Upon learning that the devotee's intention was to serve Bhagavan Shiva's followers, Idangazhi Nayanmar released him. This incident profoundly impacted the king, leading him to a realization that his wealth was not truly his own, but belonged to Bhagavan Shiva and His devotees. In a remarkable gesture of devotion and generosity, Idangazhi Nayanmar granted all devotees of Bhagavan Shiva unrestricted access to his palace and granary, allowing them to take whatever they needed. This act of selflessness and dedication to the welfare of Bhagavan Shiva's devotees greatly enhanced the spread of Shaivism and garnered divine grace for Idangazhi Nayanmar.

91e27ebf0a.d: One of the most important vratams, alongside Krishnajanmashtami, Shivaratri etc. Must observe fast. Offer Arghyam facing South, using Curd, Akshata, Water and Flowers (dadhnākṣatōdakaiḥ puṣpaiḥ) chanting the shloka mentioned. Three Vratas are very special for Subrahmanya---the bhr̥guvāra-subrahmaṇya-vratam in tulāmāsa, the regular kr̥ttikā vratam, and this most special skandaṣaṣṭhivratam.
91e27ebf0a.s:
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌸𑍁𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑍈 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌾𑌃।  
𑌤𑍁𑌲𑌾𑌰𑌾𑌶𑌿𑌂 𑌗𑌤𑍇 𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍 𑌭𑍃𑌗𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌰𑍇॥௧॥  
𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌯 𑌶𑍁𑌚𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌭𑍂𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑌰𑍇𑌵 𑌷𑌡𑌾𑌨𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌹𑍃𑌦𑌬𑍍𑌜𑌨𑌿𑌲𑌯𑍇 𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌚॥௨॥  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌚𑌰𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌹𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍍।  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑌾𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌚𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌿𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍍॥௩॥  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌣𑌿 𑌯𑍇 𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌰𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌗𑌮𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌤𑌃।  
𑌤𑍇 𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍁𑌲𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌭𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌗𑍁𑌹𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌯𑌾॥௪॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌰𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑍈𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌭𑍂𑌸𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌃।  
𑌜𑌘𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌘𑍋𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌮𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌗𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾॥௫॥  
𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌚 𑌦𑌿𑌶𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌕𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑌪𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤।  
𑌮𑍁𑌚𑍁𑌕𑍁𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍋 𑌮𑌹𑍀𑌪𑌾𑌲𑌃 𑌶𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍂𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌰𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾॥௬॥  
𑌗𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪 𑌚𑌰𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑍈𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌭𑍂𑌸𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌃।  
𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌮𑍁𑌖𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇 𑌤𑌾𑌪𑌸𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌧𑍀𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌾𑌃॥௭॥  
𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌤𑍁𑌲𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌵𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌦𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌭𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾 𑌕𑍇𑌚𑌿𑌦𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌃॥௮॥  
𑌐𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌨𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌂𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌚𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾 𑌪𑌰𑍇।  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌚𑍈𑌕𑌂 𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌰𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌹𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌮𑌤𑌮𑍍॥௯॥  
𑌸 𑌲𑌬𑍍𑌧𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌛𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌨𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌜𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌗𑍁𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌵 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌤𑌃॥௧௦॥  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌣𑌿 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌰𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌮𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌮𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑍋 𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌗𑍁𑌹𑌤𑍁𑌲𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌭𑍂𑌸𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌃॥௧௧॥   
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌰𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌉𑌪𑌦𑍇𑌶𑌕𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑍇  
  
𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌹𑌿 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍋𑌽𑌭𑌵𑌤𑍍 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑍀𑌤 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌵𑍀 𑌸𑌦𑌾॥  
  
𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌦𑌾𑌰𑌜 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌦 𑌸𑍇𑌨𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌪 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌬𑌲।  
𑌰𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌮𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌜 𑌷𑌡𑍍𑌵𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌗𑌰𑍍𑌭 𑌨𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍇॥  
  
𑌸𑍁𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌚  
𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑌾𑌶𑌨𑍋 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇 𑌨𑍃𑌪॥  
𑌰𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌚𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑍇𑌣 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌚𑌿𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍॥௧॥  
𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌾𑌜 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌦𑌾 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌾𑌮𑌦𑌾॥  
𑌉𑌪𑍋𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌂 𑌜𑌯𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌨𑌾॥௨॥  
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑌯𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌏𑌷𑌾 𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌃।  
𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌸𑍇𑌨𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌹𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌨𑌾॥௩॥  
𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌹𑌿 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌯𑌸𑌾 𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍋 𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌣𑍀𑌃।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌭𑍋𑌜𑍀 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍀𑌪𑍍𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑌦𑌾॥௪॥  
𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇𑌯𑌾𑌯 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑍈 𑌦𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌣𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌖𑌃।  
𑌦𑌧𑍍𑌨𑌾 𑌘𑍃𑌤𑍋𑌦𑌕𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌣𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑍁𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤॥௫॥  
𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌦𑌾𑌰𑌜 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌦 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌵।  
𑌰𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌜 𑌵𑌿𑌭𑍋 𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌗𑌰𑍍𑌭 𑌨𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍇।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌯𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌸𑍇𑌨𑌾𑌨𑍀𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌯𑌤𑍁 𑌹𑍃𑌦𑍍𑌗𑌤𑌮𑍍॥௬॥  
𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌯 𑌚𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌯𑌚𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌪𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇।  
𑌪𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌭𑍁𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌸𑍌 𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍌 𑌭𑍂𑌮𑌿𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌭𑌾𑌜𑌨𑌮𑍍॥௭॥  
𑌏𑌵𑌂 𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑍇𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌨 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌨𑌤𑌃।  
𑌤𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌬𑍋𑌧 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌾𑌜 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌚𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌮𑌯𑌾𑌽𑌖𑌿𑌲𑌮𑍍॥௮॥  
𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌫𑌲𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑍋 𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑍋 𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌿।  
𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌾𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌤𑍋 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌚𑌾𑌰𑍀 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌃॥௯॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌂 𑌧𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌿𑌂 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌚𑍈𑌹𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌚 𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍋 𑌨 𑌸𑌂𑌶𑌯𑌃॥௧௦॥  
𑌯𑍋 𑌹𑌿 𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌸 𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑍀 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌇𑌹 𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑍋𑌽𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑌤𑍇 𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌗𑍇 𑌚 𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌤𑌂 𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌂𑌶𑌯𑌃॥௧௧॥  
𑌇𑌹 𑌚𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌗𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌯𑌥𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌫𑌲𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌿 𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍌 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌂 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌾 𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌿॥௧௨॥  
𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌶𑍃𑌣𑍁𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌂 𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌕𑍁𑌲𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌹।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌧𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌾॥௧௩॥  
॥𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌶𑌤𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌣𑌿 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌮𑍀𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑍇 𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌨𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌏𑌕𑍋𑌨𑌚𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃॥

920fce97c6.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Caturdaśī tithi of Caitraḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
920fce97c6.d: On the Krishna Chaturdashi of Chaitra month, whoever performs snāna in a Shiva Sannidhi, or especially in Ganga, they do not atttain prētatvam.
920fce97c6.s:
𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌯𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌿𑌵𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌧𑍌।  
𑌨 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌤𑌃॥

9219860b8a.b: Observed on Paurṇamāsī tithi of Āśvayujaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti). The event occurred in 3859 (Kali era).
9219860b8a.d: Son of Somagiri, dwelling on the banks of river Pālār (Kṣīrapagā), known as Sureśa, (He) became the preceptor. A disciple of Śrī Citsukhendra, disinterest in campaigns/travels, He, on the directions of his preceptor-teacher, remained in the Maṭha itself. He, the preceptor, Śrī Citsukhānanda attained/ clung on to the state of Bliss on the day of Paurṇamī in the month of Aśvinī of the year Hevilambi. Also known as Cidānanda, He attained siddhi in Kañci itself. His preceptorship was for twenty-one years.
9219860b8a.s:
𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑍁𑌰𑍇𑌶 𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑍋𑌮𑌗𑌿𑌰𑍇𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌨𑍂𑌜𑌃 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍀𑌰𑌾𑌪𑌗𑌾𑌤𑌟𑌭𑌵𑍋𑌽𑌭𑌵𑌦𑍍 𑌆𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌮𑍀𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌃।  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍁𑌖𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌚𑌰𑌣𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌚𑌰𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌚𑌾𑌰𑌦𑍂𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌸 𑌮𑌠𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌤𑍍॥௭௦॥  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌃 𑌸𑌚𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌮𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑌦𑌮𑍍।  
𑌆𑌲𑌲𑌮𑍍𑌬𑍇 𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌲𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌣𑌿॥௭௧॥  
—𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌰𑍀

9227ea5f5f.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Aṣṭamī tithi of Mārgaśīrṣaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti).
9227ea5f5f.s:
𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌅𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌧𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌰𑍇𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌲𑌯𑌃॥  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌗𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌗𑌜𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌾𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌅𑌥𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌃। 𑌤𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌃 𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌃 - 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚 𑌶𑍌𑌨𑌕𑌃---  
𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌿𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀𑌷𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌃 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌅𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌮𑌾𑌹 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌃---  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍌𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌪𑌦𑍇 𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌿𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌰𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌇𑌤𑌿। 𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 - 𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌃, 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌃 - 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌃।  
𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---  
𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌪𑍌𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍌𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍇 𑌚 𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑍇।  
𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌰𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀।  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌤 𑌪𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌣𑌮𑍍।  
𑌆𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌾𑌯𑌨𑌃---  
𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌿𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌿 𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍈𑌃।

928484ed70.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in śravaṇaḥ makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′09.65″.
928484ed70.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′09.65″, 0°41′02.28″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 2°00′24.85″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.28, elongation 5°47′39.43″ E). śukraḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°19′15.20″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 5°35′40.29″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

9356d61040.b: Observed on Apabharaṇī nakshatra of Vr̥ṣabhaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
9356d61040.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

Kazharsinga Nayanmar, a devout follower of Bhagavan Shiva and a Pallava king from the Kadavar lineage, was instrumental in spreading Shaivism by conquering northern kingdoms. During one of his many pilgrimages, he visited the Tiruvarur temple with his queen. While circumambulating the temple, the queen unintentionally smelt a flower fallen on the ground, designated for Bhagavan Shiva's worship. Seruthunai Nayanmar, a dedicated Vellala devotee serving in the temple, saw this as a disrespectful act towards Bhagavan Shiva and impulsively cut off the queen's nose as a penalty for her indiscretion.

Alarmed by his queen's cries, King Kazharsinga rushed to the scene. Upon understanding the situation from Seruthunai Nayanmar, who explained the queen's act, the king deemed the punishment insufficient and further punished the queen by severing her hand that had touched the flower! This extreme act of devotion from both the king and Seruthunai Nayanmar was celebrated by the people, and they were showered with celestial flowers as a mark of divine approval. Both Kazharsinga Nayanmar and Seruthunai Nayanmar earned the grace of Bhagavan Shiva for their unwavering devotion. Bhagavan Shiva appeared and took Kazharsinga Nayanmar with Him, while also restoring the queen's nose and hand.
9356d61040.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society

By rashi: siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ get more ashubha phala, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, mēṣaḥ, karkaṭaḥ somewhat ashubha, tulā, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

945336a2fa.d: Devoted to Bhagavan Chandramauli, preceptor Śrī Chandraśekhara too remaining in the Pīṭha for thirty-seven years reached his eternal abode on the first day of Kṛṣṇapakṣa in the month of Kārtika of the year Sādhāraṇa. The name of this preceptor before initiation was Veñkatasubrahmaṇya Dīkṣita. He was a descendant of the family of Govinda Dīkṣita, wellknown as “Ayyan” who carried out many righteous acts of “pūrta” and adorned the ministerial post in the assembly of King Sevappa Nāyaka of the Nāyaka dynasty ruling Tanjavur. This preceptor was well-versed in Mantra Śāstra. Only during the period of this preceptor, the renovation or reinstallation of the pair of ear-rings (taṭaṅka yugala) symbolic of Srichakra, of Devī Akhilāṇdeśvarī of Jambukeśvara, renovation of Srichakra in the Kāmākṣī temple at Kāñci were carried out. During his visit ot Tanjavur, the preceptor was reverentially coronated with gold or offered Kanakābhiṣeka by the monarch who was ruling Tanjavur. Śalivahana era 1773. The adhishthanam is located at https://maps.app.goo.gl/Zrry6C2Sbqd3NUAS6, in the premises of the Kumbhaghonam Kanchi Shankara Matham.

94cc06bccf.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

Tiruneelanakka Nayanmar, the 26th of the Nayanmars, was a devout Brahmana proficient in Agamas, and resided in Tirusattamangai, a spiritually vibrant city in the Chola kingdom. Known for its dedicated Brahmanas and the temple of Ayavanthinathar (today's Brahmapureeshvarar (Ayavandheeshvarar) Svaami Temple https://maps.app.goo.gl/DHqaB7hJypLzZRUH9), this city was a centre of Shiva worship. During a Tiruvathirai festival, while Tiruneelanakka and his wife were worshiping in the temple, she instinctively blew on the Shiva Lingam to clean it from a spider, accidentally spitting on the the Shiva Lingam, an act her devout husband perceived as desecration. Angered, he abandoned her and returned home alone.

That night, Bhagavan Ayavanthinathar appeared in Tiruneelanakka's dream, showing that the part of His body his wife spat on was the only part not affected by the spider's poison, revealing the greatness of her devotion. Realising this, Tiruneelanakka Nayanmar joyously reconciled with his wife, understanding the Lingam as a living presence, not just a stone.

When the revered Tiru Jnana Sambandar (the 28th of the Nayanmars) visited Tirusattamangai with companions, Tiruneelanakka Nayanmar welcomed them but hesitated to accommodate the non-Brahmana companions inside his home, asking them to sleep near the sacrificial pit. Miraculously, the sacrificial fire ignited by itself near them, enlightening Nayanmar about the transcendence of varṇa through devotion. Sambandar, acknowledging Nayanmar's devotion, included him in a song of praise.

Yearning to be in Sambandar's presence, Tiruneelanakkar later attended Sambandar's wedding in Nallur Perumanam. When Sambandar merged into the divine light of Bhagavan Shiva, Tiruneelanakka Nayanmar also attained union with the divine, fulfilling his deepest spiritual longing.

94d13b9737.s:
𑌸𑍁𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌚  
𑌇𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾 𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌗𑍌𑌤𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌜𑌾𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌃।  
𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌣𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌨𑌾𑌗𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑍋𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑌂 𑌤𑌥𑌾॥௬௦॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌗𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌸𑌦𑌾 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌃।  
𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑌯𑌸𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌯𑌸𑍇𑌨 𑌚॥௬௧॥  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌪।  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌭𑌯𑌤𑍋 𑌲𑍇𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌗𑍋𑌮𑌯𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍋𑌲𑍍𑌬𑌣𑌾𑌃॥௬௨॥  
𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌂 𑌦𑌧𑌿𑌦𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌤𑍈𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌶𑍈𑌃।  
𑌗𑌨𑍍𑌧𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑍋𑌪𑌹𑌾𑌰𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌤𑌰𑍍𑌪𑌣𑍈𑌃॥௬௩॥  
𑌯𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍀𑌹 𑌨𑌾𑌗𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌃𑌸𑌰𑌾𑌃।  
𑌨 𑌤𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍋 𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌭𑌯𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑌤𑌿 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌿𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍॥௬௪॥  
॥𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌶𑌤𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌣𑌿 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌮𑍀𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑍇 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑌿𑌕𑌨𑌾𑌗𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌮𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌨𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌷𑌟𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃॥  
𑌅𑌪𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌪 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌪 𑌭𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑍂𑌰𑌂 𑌗𑌚𑍍𑌛 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌯𑌶𑌾𑌃।  
𑌜𑌨𑌮𑍇𑌜𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍀𑌕𑌵𑌚𑌨𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌰𑌨𑍍॥

---𑌵𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 (𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍌𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌭𑌮𑍍)

---𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍌𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌭𑍇  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌕𑌰𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌵𑌾𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌹 𑌶𑌾𑌤𑌾𑌤𑌪𑌃—  
𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃।  
𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌸𑍁 𑌰𑍋𑌗𑍀 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌦𑍁𑌃𑌖𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍀 𑌚 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌹𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑍈𑌃।  
𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑌦𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌃 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌸𑍁 𑌨𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍॥  
---𑌵𑍈𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌨𑌾𑌥-𑌦𑍀𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑍇 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌫𑌲𑍇 𑌆𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌕-𑌕𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌃 (𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌃)  
𑌅𑌤𑍀𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌗𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍇 𑌉𑌦𑌗𑍍𑌦𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌣𑌾𑌯𑌨𑍇।  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑍍𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌟𑌕𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌡𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑌕𑌰𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌨𑌾𑌡𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
---𑌵𑍈𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌨𑌾𑌥-𑌦𑍀𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑍇 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌫𑌲𑍇 𑌆𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌕-𑌕𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌃 (𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌃)

956b2c079f.b: Observed on Śukla-Prathamā tithi of Māghaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
956b2c079f.d: Māgha-māsaḥ begins today --- special for various dānam's and especially māghasnānam! As stated by Viṣṇu: In the month of Māgha, one should daily offer oblations into the fire using sesame seeds mixed with ghee, and feed brāhmaṇas with kṛsarānna (sweet rice with ghee) or śarkarānna (sugar rice). Such a person becomes radiant. In the Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa, it is said that one should perform daily ritual baths for 30 days, as long as the Sun remains in Makara, beginning on the full moon or new moon (thus, both amānta and purṇimānta māsās have pramāṇa). These baths bring great merit! In the Vāmana Purāṇa, it is stated that a person who bathes in cold water during Māgha earns the merit of an aśvamedha sacrifice with every step! After completing the bath, one should offer unrestricted food to a brāhmaṇa couple and adorn them with garments and ornaments. The Vāmana Purāṇa states that in Māgha, dāna of sesame seeds and a tila-dhenu is highly meritorious. Similarly, donations of firewood and other essentials should be done to please Mādhava.
956b2c079f.s:
𑌦𑍇𑌵𑍈𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌜𑌃 𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌂 𑌜𑌲𑍇।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌜𑌲𑌂 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇 𑌪𑌾𑌵𑌨𑌂 𑌹𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌤𑌃॥  
---𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌉𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑍇 ௩௧.௧௦  
𑌤𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌕𑌂 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌨 𑌶𑍋𑌧𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌅𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍇𑌶𑌾𑌦𑌧𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑍋𑌷𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌵 𑌮𑌜𑍍𑌜𑌨𑌮𑍍॥  
---𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌉𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑍇 ௩௧.௧௬  
𑌪𑌾𑌵𑌕𑌾 𑌇𑌵 𑌦𑍀𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌨𑌰𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌃।  
𑌵𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌪𑌾𑌪𑍇𑌭𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑍇𑌘𑍇𑌭𑍍𑌯 𑌇𑌵 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌃॥  
---𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌉𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 ௧௨௬.௩௨  
𑌏𑌕𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌕𑍁𑌲𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌭𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌯𑌥𑍇𑌪𑍍𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍।  
𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌷𑌸𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌂 𑌸 𑌗𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌿॥  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌉𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌣𑌿 ௧௨௨.௩௪  
𑌕𑌾𑌵𑍇𑌰𑍀 𑌤𑍁𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌭𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌚 𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌗𑌾𑌃।  
𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌯𑍀 𑌨𑌰𑍋 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌮𑌷𑌃॥  
---𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌉𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑍇 ௬௩.௩௦  
  
𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌮𑍍---  
𑌤𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌰𑍍𑌕𑍋𑌦𑌯𑍇 𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌹𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌮𑍍।  
𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵𑌾𑌯 𑌦𑌦𑌾𑌮𑍀𑌦𑌮𑍍 𑌅𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌧𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥-𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌦𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵𑌾𑌯 𑌨𑌮𑌃 𑌇𑌦𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍। 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵𑌾𑌯 𑌨𑌮𑌃 𑌇𑌦𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍। 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵𑌾𑌯 𑌨𑌮𑌃 𑌇𑌦𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
  
𑌸𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌚 𑌪𑌰𑌂 𑌧𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌨𑍇 𑌨𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍇।  
𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌜𑌸𑌾 𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌧𑌾॥  
𑌸𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌮𑌃 𑌇𑌦𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍। 𑌸𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌮𑌃 𑌇𑌦𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍। 𑌸𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌮𑌃 𑌇𑌦𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
  
𑌯𑌦𑌨𑍇𑌕𑌜𑌨𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌯𑌜𑍍𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌨𑌤𑌃 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌜𑌸𑌾 𑌹𑌤𑌂 𑌚𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌂 𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌧𑌾॥  
𑌸𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌮𑌃 𑌇𑌦𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍। 𑌸𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌮𑌃 𑌇𑌦𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍। 𑌸𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌮𑌃 𑌇𑌦𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌨𑌾---  
𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌾𑌕𑌰 𑌜𑌗𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌥 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌕𑌰 𑌨𑌮𑍋𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍇।  
𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌂 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌮𑍍॥  
  
𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌹 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌃---  
𑌮𑌾𑌘𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌹𑌂 𑌤𑌿𑌲𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌹𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑌘𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌸𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌂/𑌶𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌂 𑌬𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌭𑍋𑌜𑌯𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍀𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌤𑌿।  
𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌪𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌮𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑌭𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌮𑌾𑌚𑌰𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌮𑌕𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌥𑍇 𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌾𑌕𑌰𑍇॥  
𑌵𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌅𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑍃𑌤𑌶𑌰𑍀𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌯𑌃 𑌕𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌮𑌾𑌚𑌰𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌪𑌦𑍇 𑌪𑌦𑍇𑌽𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌧𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃॥  
𑌏𑌵𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌸𑌾𑌨𑍇 𑌭𑍋𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌯𑌮𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌭𑍋𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌦𑍍 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌦𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌭𑍂𑌷𑌯𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌭𑍂𑌷𑌣𑍈𑌃॥  
𑌵𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌮𑌾𑌘𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌤𑌿𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌶𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌲𑌧𑍇𑌨𑍁𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌤𑌃।

95ad464f7c.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in viśākhā tulā, center-to-center separation 0°59′14.64″.
95ad464f7c.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°59′14.64″, 0°59′04.97″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 1°53′49.22″ N, vakra (retrograde), magnitude +2.08, elongation 10°27′48.56″ W). śukraḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 0°54′34.58″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.92, elongation 10°19′53.82″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

96276e937c.d:
Uttarāyaṇa-puṇyakālaḥ. For uttarāyaṇa, the 20 ghatikas succeeding the saṅkramaṇa form a puṇyakāla; in general, the ghatikas closer to the puṇyakāla are even more sacred.

While the nirayana puṇyakāla-s are well known, marked by the transit of the Sun into various rāśī-s (which confer the name to the corresponding saura month), there are also ayana-s and sāyana saṅkramaṇa-s, which mark the position of the Sun above the Northern or Southern parts of the Earth. These determine the r̥tu-s, and also the very famous uttarāyaṇa and dakṣināyana (movement of the Sun towards North or South, respectively). While these two types of puṇyakāla-s (sāyana and nirayana) coincided millennia ago, there has been a gradual precession of the equinoxes, owing to the nature of the Earth's rotation, causing the sāyana saṅkramaṇa-s to happen about 24 days before the nirayana saṅkramaṇa-s. In that era, uttarāyaṇa coincided with makara-saṅkramaṇa and dakṣināyana coincided with karkaṭaka-saṅkramaṇa, and the mēsa and tulā saṅkramaṇa-s corresponded to the equinoxes, when the Sun rises direct East (and sets direct West).

Many Dharma Shastra texts recognise the separate puṇyakāla-s for both types of saṅkramaṇa-s. The vachanam of Jaabaali Maharshi is mentioned above, where he says that the puṇyakāla-s are identical (in their reckoning) for both types of saṅkramaṇa-s. In Kala Madhava, which is considered as the source text of the kala vicharas of the Dikshitiya, it is said in the 5th prakarana that,  meṣādi-saṅkrāntayo yasmin dine bhavanti tasmād dināt pūrvebhyaḥ ekādaśabhyo dinebhyaḥ prācīne dine, noting that Sayana Sankramanas occurred ~11 days before the day when the Mesha Sankramanas etc occur. Further references are seen in Dharma Sindhu first pariccheda, Jayasimha Kalpadruma sankranti nirnaya and Nirnaya Sindhu first pariccheda. There are also ample references in Vedas, illustrating how Ayana-s happened much later (in certain other eras), e.g. Shukla Yajur Veda Shatapatha Brahmana (Ekapaat Kanda 1/2/3), Nakshatra Sukta belonging to the Atharva Veda (Shaunaka Samhita 19/7/2), Maitrayaniya Aranyaka (6/14), and Taittiriya Brahmana (1/5/2).

For a wonderfully detailed exposition on the topic, see https://sites.google.com/view/nakshatradarsha/dakshinayana-en and https://sites.google.com/view/nakshatradarsha/uttarayana-en .

---𑌵𑍈𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌨𑌾𑌥-𑌦𑍀𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑍇 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌫𑌲𑍇 𑌆𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌕-𑌕𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌃 (𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌃)  
𑌜𑌾𑌬𑌾𑌲𑌿𑌃---  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌦𑍀𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌯𑌨𑍇 𑌤𑌥𑌾।

96419d6726.b: Partial solar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈1.7 of 12 aṅgulas), Sun at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
96419d6726.d: Magnitude: 14% of the solar diameter is covered (parimāṇa ≈1.7 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 02:27►17:12 (from 4 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra punarvasuḥ/puṣyaḥ/āśrēṣā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or anūrādhā (anujanma) or uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: karkaṭaḥ, siṁhaḥ, dhanuḥ, mēṣaḥ get more ashubha phala, vr̥śchikaḥ, makaraḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam somewhat ashubha, kanyā, tulā, kumbhaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
96419d6726.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

9698c5c29e.b: Observed on Śukla-Daśamī tithi of Jyaiṣṭhaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti). The event occurred in 3476 (Kali era).
9698c5c29e.d: The one who was born to a brahmin Śrīdeva Miśrā; soon after the birth uttered the Truth that ‘everything is Ātman’ due to the samskāras of the previous birth; the Buddhists and Jains unable to counter the doctrine threw him in the river Sindhu, who saved his life by placing him lovingly on the lotus petals. Being carried by her (river Sindhu) He (Sadāśivabāla) was given to a brahmin endowed with austerities saying “pleased by your austerities/penance today this boy/child is given”; then being asked/enquired by Bhūrivasu of Pushpapura and initiated by him—the saviour—father, He held high the school of nondualism. Preceptor Śrī Sadāśivabāla having served with reverence Śrī Ujjvala Śaṅkarācārya, got initiation, adhering to the principles of asceticism well carried out voyage in palanquin. Preceptor Sadāśiva, always intent on feeding one thousand brahmins, moved around everywhere imparted as per injunctions, for fifty times and governing the maṭha of the Universal Preceptor for eight years, then installing Surendra spent sometime, reached the tranquil state in Tamaraparni (He attained jivasamadhi in Triyambakeshwar.). Sadāśiva, the great among ascetics, the personification of Bhagavan Śiva, the accomplished One, attained his final beatitude on the tenth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Jyeṣṭha of the year Bhava.
9698c5c29e.s:
𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌮𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌅𑌜𑌨𑌿 𑌜𑌨𑌿𑌤 𑌏𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑌾𑌶𑌃  
𑌸𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌨𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑌗𑌿𑌰𑌤 𑌗𑌿𑌰𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍍 𑌆𑌤𑍍𑌮𑍇𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
𑌤𑌨𑍍𑌨𑍋 𑌮𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌿𑌰𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌜𑍍𑌜𑌿𑌨𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌭𑌿𑌜𑌨𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍁𑌵𑍇𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌮𑍍𑌣𑍈𑌵 𑌸𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌵𑌿𑌲𑌯𑌮𑍍 𑌅𑌮𑍁𑌯𑌾 𑌪𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌿𑌵𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌯॥௩௪॥  
𑌸𑍂𑌨𑍁𑌃 𑌸𑍋𑌽𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑌪𑍋𑌭𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌵 𑌮𑍁𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌧𑌿𑌯𑌾 𑌦𑍀𑌯𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑌾𑌚𑌾  
𑌸𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌾𑌯 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌰𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍇 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌯𑍈𑌵𑍋𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌃।  
𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌨𑌾𑌥 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌭𑌿𑌧𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌜𑌨𑍁𑌷𑌾 𑌭𑍂𑌰𑌿𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍇𑌨  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌪𑌨𑍀𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑌯𑌮𑍍 𑌅𑌯𑌮𑍍 𑌅𑌧𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌅𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌯𑌂 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌵𑍇॥௩௫॥  
𑌆𑌚𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍 𑌉𑌜𑍍𑌜𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌯𑌤𑌿𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍   
𑌆𑌰𑌾𑌧𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌂𑌯𑌮𑌮𑍍 𑌅𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌦𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌯𑍈𑌵।  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌸𑌦𑌾𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌧𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌽𑌬𑍍𑌧𑌿 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌂  
𑌸𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍋𑌲𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌸𑍁𑌵𑌿𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌧𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌃॥௩௬॥  
𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌪𑍋𑌷𑌣𑌪𑌰𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌭𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍋𑌃  
𑌸𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌸𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑌂 𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌾𑌂𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌶𑌤𑌃।  
𑌅𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟 𑌜𑌗𑌦𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍋𑌰𑌧𑌿𑌮𑌠𑌂 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌲𑍀𑌂  
𑌜𑍀𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌨𑍇𑌵 𑌸𑌦𑌾𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑌵𑌿𑌶𑌤𑍍 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑍁𑌰𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌦𑍇॥௩௭॥  
𑌭𑌵𑍇 𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌸𑍋𑌽𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇 𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍇 𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌦𑌶𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍍 𑌆𑌪 𑌦𑌶𑌮𑍀𑌂 𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌂 𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌃 𑌸𑌦𑌾𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌃॥௩௮॥  
—𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌰𑍀

96a9315a03.d: On the kr̥ṣṇa-pakṣa-tr̥tīyā days in the months of āṣāḍha, kārtika and phālguna, one must not perform adhyayana, as also on āśvayuk-śukla-dvitīyā.
96a9315a03.s:
𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇—  
𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑌾𑌷𑌾𑌢𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇।  
𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍁𑌗𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑍈𑌵𑌾𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌚𑌰𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋𑌽𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌨𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌧𑍀𑌯𑍀𑌤 𑌕𑌦𑌾𑌚𑌨।

96e76df650.d: The Tiruchendur Brahmotsavam of Avani each year is very special. The festival is conducted for twelve days. This marks the eighth day of the festival. A unique decoration on this day is the most beautiful 'pachai satthi alankaram'.

96fa1493c7.b: Observed on Svātī nakshatra of Karkaṭaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
96fa1493c7.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

Sundaramurti Nayanmar, born around 800 CE to parents who were themselves Nayanmars (chaḍaiya nāyanmār (62) and ichaiñāniyār nāyanmār (63)). He contributed the seventh volume of Thirumurai with his hymns. His life took a dramatic turn during his wedding, when an elderly ascetic adorned with sacred ash and rudraksha beads disrupted the ceremony. The ascetic claimed Sundarar as his servant, presenting a palm-leaf manuscript as evidence. Initially, Sundarar dismissed him as a 'pitthan' (madman). However, the authenticity of the palm leaf was confirmed, leading Sundarar to follow the ascetic to the Thiruvennainallur Shiva temple. There, the ascetic vanished into the inner sanctum. 

Bhagavan Shiva then appeared, requesting Sundarar to compose a hymn starting with the term ‘pitthan’, which he had used earlier. Sundarar's inaugural hymn, “Pittha pirai choodi” (O crazy one wearing the crescent moon), was dedicated to the deity at the Tiru Arul Turai Temple (now known as Kripapureeswarar Perumal Temple). This temple was one of the 82 Shiva temples he visited during his brief lifespan of just 18 years. Despite his short life, Sundarar's contributions significantly enriched Tamil Shaiva literature, marking him as a prominent Nayanmar.
96fa1493c7.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society

97239f7a29.b: Observed on Śukla-Pañcamī tithi of Bhādrapadaḥ (lunar) month (Madhyāhnaḥ/puurvaviddha).
97239f7a29.s:
𑌭𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌦𑍃𑌷𑌿𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍॥௩௪॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑌰𑍍𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑍇 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌤𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌃।  
𑌗𑍃𑌹𑌮𑌾𑌗𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌯𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌦𑌾॥௩௫॥  
𑌗𑍋𑌮𑌯𑍇𑌨𑍋𑌪𑌲𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌥 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑍋𑌪𑌶𑍋𑌭𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑍁𑌶𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰 𑌋𑌷𑍀𑌨𑍍𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤 𑌸𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௩௬॥  
𑌗𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌧𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌧𑍂𑌪𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍀𑌪𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑍁𑌶𑍋𑌭𑌨𑍈𑌃।  
𑌕𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍋𑌽𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌰𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌜𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌮𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌥 𑌗𑍌𑌤𑌮𑌃॥௩௭॥  
𑌜𑌮𑌦𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌸𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑍈𑌤𑍇 𑌋𑌷𑌯𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌾𑌃।  
𑌏𑌤𑍇𑌭𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌯𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌾𑌯 𑌚॥௩௮॥  
𑌨𑍈𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑌚𑌦𑍍𑌦𑍀𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌕𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌰𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑍈𑌃।  
𑌤𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌿𑌸𑍃𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌯𑌂 𑌚𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌦𑍇𑌵 𑌹𑌿॥௩௯॥  
𑌅𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿𑌨𑌾 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌰𑌮𑍍।  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌵𑌰𑌯𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌚𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤 𑌵𑍈𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍॥௪௦॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌤 𑌸𑍁𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌃।  
𑌜𑌟𑌿𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌸𑍂𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌕𑌮𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌲𑍁𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥௪௧॥  
𑌸𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑌶𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌤𑌾𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌮𑍃𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌯𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌵𑌾।  
𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑌯𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿 𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌪𑍃𑌥𑌕𑍍 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍈𑌰𑌪𑌿॥௪௨॥  
𑌉𑌪𑌚𑌾𑌰𑍈𑌃 𑌷𑍋𑌡𑌶𑌭𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌃।  
𑌅𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌤𑌤𑍋 𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌂 𑌤𑌿𑌲𑌵𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌹𑌿𑌯𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌃॥௪௩॥  
`𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍋𑌮𑌾' 𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌋𑌚𑌾 𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍃𑌥𑌕𑍍।  
𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌹𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌹𑍁𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌚𑌰𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௪௪॥  
𑌤𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤 𑌗𑌾 𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌲𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌸𑌂𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌾𑌃।  
𑌆𑌚𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌚𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌲𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌭𑍂𑌷𑌣𑍈𑌃॥௪௫॥  
𑌅𑌨𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌯𑌾 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍋𑌃 𑌪𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌮𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌚𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌪𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌭𑍋𑌜𑌯𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌿𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌿𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௪௬॥  
𑌤𑌤𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑌹𑌾𑌸𑍀𑌨𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌯𑌂 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑍈 𑌷𑌡𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍋𑌪𑍇𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌹 𑌬𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍁𑌭𑌿𑌃॥௪௭॥  
𑌏𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌂𑌶𑍍 𑌭𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌥 𑌵𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌛𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍।  
𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍍𑌷𑍀𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌰𑌗𑍋 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௪௮॥

978fd4ad38.d: On this day, From Wākharī, both the Āl̤andī and Dehu Pālkhīs—along with hundreds of others from across Maharashtra—walk the final stretch together to Panḍharpur. On this holy day of Ashadhi Ekadashi, the Wāri culminates. The pilgrims take a holy dip in the Chandrabhāgā river and complete the Pradakshina of the Vithoba temple, and of course, darshan of Bhagavan Viṭhobā, fulfilling their vow of the Wari.

9792ddd49c.d: Budhaḥ sets into combustion (astamayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2026-Dec-11 00:40. At this moment budhaḥ is at anūrādhā-3 vr̥śchikaḥ (latitude 0°22′35.19″ N, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -0.69, elongation 11°58′42.59″ W of the Sun. Combustion (mAudhyam) is generally considered to weaken a graha's ability to give full results in its significations; undertakings connected with budhaḥ are traditionally best avoided until it re-emerges.

97a69251ab.b: Observed on Paurṇamāsī tithi of Śrāvaṇaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti). The event occurred in 3538 (Kali era).
97a69251ab.d: Dumb boy, as He was named born of Khalvāṭavīra, the gem in the family of gaṇakas, got the ability to speak eloquently through the greatness of (the grace of) the Universal Preceptor, invested with sacred thread, and initiated into the entire scripture by his father and taking up asceticism, He remained in the seat of Universal preceptor. Preceptor Śaṅkarendra (Arbhakaśaṅkara), after installing Mātṛgupta, the ardent follower of the precepts of varṇāśrama (enjoined for respective classes of people) attained Siddhi on the full moon day in the month of Śravaṇa of the Śaka year 359. (In the Sanskrit and Tamil explanations on Pages 22 & 23, Matrugupta appears to be a patron of Sankarendra along with Ramilla, Sri Harsha etc.)
97a69251ab.s:
𑌜𑌾𑌤𑌃 𑌖𑌲𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌟𑌵𑍀𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌗𑌣𑌕𑌕𑍁𑌲𑌮𑌣𑍇𑌃 𑌸𑌾𑌧𑍁 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌤𑍀𑌤𑍋  
𑌮𑍂𑌕𑍋 𑌮𑍂𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌾 𑌭𑍁𑌵𑌨𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌪𑌦𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌭𑍋𑌜𑌰𑍇𑌣𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌹𑌿𑌮𑍍𑌨𑌾।  
𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍌𑌢𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌪𑌨𑌯𑌨𑌮𑌖𑌿𑌲𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌯𑌜𑌾𑌤𑌂 𑌚 𑌤𑌾𑌤𑌾𑌦𑍍  
𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍍𑌣𑌨𑍍 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑌮𑍍 𑌆𑌸𑍀𑌤𑍍 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍍 𑌅𑌧𑌿𑌜𑌗𑌦𑌾𑌚𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍀𑌠𑌂 𑌸 𑌧𑍀𑌰𑌃॥௪௩॥  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍃𑌗𑍁𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍍 𑌆𑌧𑌾𑌯 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌧𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌪𑌾𑌲𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑍈𑌕𑍋𑌨𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌶𑌤𑍇 𑌶𑌕𑍇𑌽𑌬𑍍𑌦𑍇 𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌂 𑌗𑌤𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍍॥௪௪॥  
—𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌰𑍀

97a90b6b51.b: Observed on Uttaraprōṣṭhapadā nakshatra of Kumbhaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha). The event occurred in 5008 (Kali era).
97a90b6b51.d: Jagadguru śrī~chandraśēkharēndra sarasvatī 7 was inducted into sannyāsāśramam on Friday, 15th February 1907, parābhava year, kumbha/adhika phālguna māsa śukla tr̥tīyā bhr̥guvāsaraḥ uttaraprōṣṭhapadā nakṣatram.

97aa73eeff.d: Guruḥ emerges from combustion into bAlya (infancy) on 2027-Sep-14 08:49. At this moment guruḥ is at pūrvaphalgunī-1 siṁhaḥ (latitude 0°56′03.51″ N, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -1.70, elongation 10°27′44.74″ W of the Sun. A graha in bAlya is likewise considered to give reduced results, for 15 days, before regaining its full strength.

97c9954498.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Aṣṭamī tithi of Pauṣaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti).
97c9954498.s:
𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌅𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌧𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌰𑍇𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌲𑌯𑌃॥  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌗𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌗𑌜𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌾𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌅𑌥𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌃। 𑌤𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌃 𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌃 - 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚 𑌶𑍌𑌨𑌕𑌃---  
𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌿𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀𑌷𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌃 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌅𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌮𑌾𑌹 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌃---  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍌𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌪𑌦𑍇 𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌿𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌰𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌇𑌤𑌿। 𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 - 𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌃, 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌃 - 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌃।  
𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---  
𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌪𑍌𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍌𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍇 𑌚 𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑍇।  
𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌰𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀।  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌤 𑌪𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌣𑌮𑍍।  
𑌆𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌾𑌯𑌨𑌃---  
𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌿𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌿 𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍈𑌃।  
𑌸𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍈𑌰𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀𑌷𑍁 𑌚।   
𑌏𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌹𑌿 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌨𑌾 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌬𑍋𑌧𑌾𑌯𑌨𑍋𑌽𑌪𑌿---  
𑌉𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌅𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿𑌤𑌿 𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑍇𑌤𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
  
𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍀𑌯𑌂 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍌𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌪𑌦𑍇 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌃।  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌥𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌬𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍂𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍॥௧௯॥  
𑌅𑌯𑌨𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍁𑌵𑍇 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍀𑌪𑌾𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑍇।  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌗𑍇 𑌚 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌣𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌚॥௨௦॥  
𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌥 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇।  
𑌚𑌤𑌸𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌵𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌶𑌿𑌶𑌿𑌰𑍇 𑌤𑌥𑌾॥௨௧॥  
𑌮𑌾𑌘𑍇 𑌚 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌘𑌾𑌰𑌾𑌕𑌾𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌗𑌮𑍇।  
𑌰𑌾𑌕𑌯𑌾 𑌚𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌚 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌪𑌿॥௨௨॥  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌨𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌧𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌣𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰 𑌉𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌃।  
𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌣𑌯𑍋𑌗𑍂𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍॥௨௩॥  
𑌤 𑌏𑌤𑍇 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌯𑌸𑌃 𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾 𑌨𑍃𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌯𑍋𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌨𑌾𑌃।  
𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌨𑍈𑌤𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌮𑍋𑌘𑌂 𑌤𑌦𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌷𑌃॥௨௪॥  
𑌏𑌷𑍁 𑌸𑍍‍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌜𑌪𑍋 𑌹𑍋𑌮𑍋 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍃𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌨𑍃𑌭𑍂𑌤𑍇𑌭𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌯𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌨𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌮𑍍॥௨௫॥  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌮𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌵𑌤𑍇 ௭-௧௪

97d5946e35.d:
The Krishna-paksha Ekadashi of āṣāḍha month is known as kāmikā-ēkādaśī.

The fruits of fasting on Ekādaśī are greatly extolled in the Padma Purana—

A person who bathes at Śaṃkhoddhāra and beholds the image of Viṣṇu does not acquire even a sixteenth of the merit earned by fasting on Ekādaśī. O noble king, even if one gives four lakhs of coins on the days of the Sun's transition between Zodiac signs, it does not equal even a sixteenth of the merit from an Ekādaśī fast! Indeed, fasting on Ekādaśī grants the same religious merit as bathing at Prabhāsa during a lunar or solar eclipse. One who drinks the sacred water at Kedāra is freed from rebirth, and likewise, fasting on Ekādaśī removes the cycle of rebirth.

The merit from an Ekādaśī fast is a hundred times greater than the reward of performing an Ashvamedha sacrifice on earth. Fasting on Ekādaśī yields a hundredfold more merit than gifting a thousand cows to a learned brāhmaṇa. Those who fast on Ekādaśī are considered equal to those whose bodies are inhabited by Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. The merit from observing the Ekādaśī vow is immeasurable, and difficult to obtain even by the Devas. There is no other vow like that of the Ekādaśī, that destroys sins.
97d5946e35.s:
𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌪𑍋𑌷𑌣𑌮𑍍।  
𑌯𑌦𑍀𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌸𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌨𑌃।  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑍀𑌤 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑍋𑌰𑍁𑌭𑌯𑍋𑌰𑌪𑌿॥  
  
𑌅𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌭𑍂𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰।  
𑌭𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌰𑍀𑌕𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷 𑌶𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌮𑍇 𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌦𑌥𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌲𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌰𑍇 𑌕𑍇𑌶𑌵 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵।  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌵𑍈 𑌵𑌿𑌘𑍍𑌨𑍋 𑌨 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌤𑌃॥  
--𑌪𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇  
  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑍈𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌸𑍌𑌤𑌿𑌶𑍌𑌨𑌕𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑍋𑌪𑌦𑍇𑌶𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃---  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌂 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍀 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇।  
𑌸 𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍈𑌕𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌠𑍇 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍈 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑍋 𑌵𑌯𑌃॥௧௪॥  
  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌂 𑌗𑌦𑌾𑌧𑌰𑌮𑍍॥௩௫॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌤𑌿 𑌷𑍋𑌡𑌶𑍀𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑍃𑌪𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮॥௩௬॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌤𑌿 𑌷𑍋𑌡𑌶𑍀𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌣𑍇 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌯𑍋𑌃॥௩௭॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑍂𑌨𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌕𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌰𑍇 𑌚𑍋𑌦𑌕𑌂 𑌪𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮 𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇॥௩௮॥  
𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌪𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥 𑌗𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑍀।  
𑌅𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌧𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍃𑌥𑌿𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௩௯॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌤𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌨𑍋 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍇 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌤𑍇 𑌚 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌃॥௪௦॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑍂𑌨𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌗𑍋𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌣 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌪𑌾𑌰𑌗𑍇॥௪௧॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌯𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌹𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌮𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌾𑌃॥௪௨॥  
𑌵𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍇 𑌤𑍁𑌲𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍋 𑌯𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌕𑌾𑌃॥௪௩॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇।  
𑌏𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍁𑌰𑍈𑌰𑌪𑌿 𑌦𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌭𑌮𑍍॥௪௪॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌸𑌮𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌾𑌶𑌨𑌮𑍍॥௧௧௮॥  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌶𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌉𑌮𑌾𑌮𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿-𑌮𑍁𑌰𑌵𑌧𑍋 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌚𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃॥௪௦॥

97eb0ecfc0.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in śravaṇaḥ makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′09.48″.
97eb0ecfc0.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′09.48″, 0°41′02.12″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 2°00′23.93″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.28, elongation 5°47′39.47″ E). śukraḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°19′14.45″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 5°35′40.32″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

98b5a0252b.d:
The Shukla-paksha Ekadashi of mārgaśīrṣa month is known as mōkṣadā-ēkādaśī. During the bright half of Mārgaśīrṣa, the Mokṣadā Ekādaśī vratam is observed, and it is recommended that its religious merits be dedicated to deceased ancestors for their salvation, as stated by Brahmā. King Vaikhānasa, after hearing a sage's advice, returned home and observed this vow during Mārgaśīrṣa. Just as he dedicated its merits to his father, a shower of flowers fell from the sky, leading to a miracle --- celestial event where flowers showered from the sky, and Vaikhānasa's father and ancestors attained salvation! From the heavens, the father blessed his son and ascended to the divine realm. Observing the Mokṣadā Ekādaśī vratam eradicates sins and grants salvation after death. This Ekādaśī is deemed unparalleled in its ability to offer salvation. The extent of its religious merit is immeasurable, likened to a wish-fulfilling gem. Simply reading or hearing of this vratam bestows religious merit comparable to that of a Vājapeya sacrifice.

The fruits of fasting on Ekādaśī are greatly extolled in the Padma Purana—

A person who bathes at Śaṃkhoddhāra and beholds the image of Viṣṇu does not acquire even a sixteenth of the merit earned by fasting on Ekādaśī. O noble king, even if one gives four lakhs of coins on the days of the Sun's transition between Zodiac signs, it does not equal even a sixteenth of the merit from an Ekādaśī fast! Indeed, fasting on Ekādaśī grants the same religious merit as bathing at Prabhāsa during a lunar or solar eclipse. One who drinks the sacred water at Kedāra is freed from rebirth, and likewise, fasting on Ekādaśī removes the cycle of rebirth.

The merit from an Ekādaśī fast is a hundred times greater than the reward of performing an Ashvamedha sacrifice on earth. Fasting on Ekādaśī yields a hundredfold more merit than gifting a thousand cows to a learned brāhmaṇa. Those who fast on Ekādaśī are considered equal to those whose bodies are inhabited by Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. The merit from observing the Ekādaśī vow is immeasurable, and difficult to obtain even by the Devas. There is no other vow like that of the Ekādaśī, that destroys sins.

𑌯𑌦𑍀𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌸𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌨𑌃।

𑌅𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌭𑍂𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰।  
𑌭𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌰𑍀𑌕𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷 𑌶𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌮𑍇 𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌦𑌥𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌲𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌰𑍇 𑌕𑍇𑌶𑌵 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵।  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌵𑍈 𑌵𑌿𑌘𑍍𑌨𑍋 𑌨 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌤𑌃॥  
--𑌪𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇  
  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑍈𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌸𑍌𑌤𑌿𑌶𑍌𑌨𑌕𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑍋𑌪𑌦𑍇𑌶𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃---  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌂 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍀 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇।  
𑌸 𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍈𑌕𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌠𑍇 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍈 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑍋 𑌵𑌯𑌃॥௧௪॥  
  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌂 𑌗𑌦𑌾𑌧𑌰𑌮𑍍॥௩௫॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌤𑌿 𑌷𑍋𑌡𑌶𑍀𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑍃𑌪𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮॥௩௬॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌤𑌿 𑌷𑍋𑌡𑌶𑍀𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌣𑍇 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌯𑍋𑌃॥௩௭॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑍂𑌨𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌕𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌰𑍇 𑌚𑍋𑌦𑌕𑌂 𑌪𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮 𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇॥௩௮॥  
𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌪𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥 𑌗𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑍀।  
𑌅𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌧𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍃𑌥𑌿𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௩௯॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌤𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌨𑍋 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍇 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌤𑍇 𑌚 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌃॥௪௦॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑍂𑌨𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌗𑍋𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌣 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌪𑌾𑌰𑌗𑍇॥௪௧॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌯𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌹𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌮𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌾𑌃॥௪௨॥  
𑌵𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍇 𑌤𑍁𑌲𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍋 𑌯𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌕𑌾𑌃॥௪௩॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇।  
𑌏𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍁𑌰𑍈𑌰𑌪𑌿 𑌦𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌭𑌮𑍍॥௪௪॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌸𑌮𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌾𑌶𑌨𑌮𑍍॥௧௧௮॥  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌶𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌉𑌮𑌾𑌮𑌹𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿-𑌮𑍁𑌰𑌵𑌧𑍋 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌚𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃॥௪௦॥  
𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾 𑌨𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌤𑌃।  
𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍇𑌤𑌦𑍍 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑍀𑌯𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍॥௩௯॥  
𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌵𑍇𑌨 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌿।  
𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌤𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌗 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑍋 𑌵𑌚𑌨𑌂 𑌯𑌥𑌾॥௪௦॥  
𑌮𑍁𑌨𑍇𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑌤𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌗𑍃𑌹𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌗𑌤𑌃।  
𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌕𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍇𑌨 𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑍈॥௪௧॥  
𑌮𑍁𑌨𑍇𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌨 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌵𑍈𑌖𑌾𑌨𑌸𑍋 𑌨𑍃𑌪𑌃।  
𑌅𑌦𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌖𑌿𑌲𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌸 𑌭𑍂𑌮𑌿𑌪𑌃॥௪௨॥  
𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌣𑍇𑌨𑍈𑌵 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑌵𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌿𑌰𑌭𑍂𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌿।  
𑌵𑍈𑌖𑌾𑌨𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌾𑌤𑍋 𑌵𑍈 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍃𑌭𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌶𑌤𑍍॥௪௩॥  
𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌚𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌿𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌸 𑌗𑌿𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌚 𑌹।  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍀𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌚𑍍𑌯 𑌚𑍈𑌵𑌂 𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌂 𑌗𑌤𑌃॥௪௪॥  
𑌏𑌵𑌂 𑌯𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌤𑍇 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌨𑍍 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌂 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌨𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍋 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌮𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍॥௪௫॥  
𑌨𑌾𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑌰𑌤𑌰𑌾 𑌕𑌾𑌚𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌦𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨 𑌜𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌨𑍍 𑌮𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌕𑍃𑌦𑍍 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌮𑍍॥௪௬॥  
𑌚𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌮𑌣𑌿𑌸𑌮𑌾 𑌹𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌷𑌾 𑌨𑍃𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌾𑌯𑌿𑌨𑍀।  
𑌪𑌠𑌨𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌣𑌾𑌦𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌵𑌾𑌜𑌪𑍇𑌯𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௪௭॥  
---𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣 𑌉𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡 𑌉𑌮𑌾𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌷-𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲-𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌦𑌾 𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌨𑌾𑌮𑍈𑌕𑌚𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃

98cd7a5b54.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Aṣṭamī tithi of Kārttikaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti). The event occurred in 4079 (Kali era).
98cd7a5b54.d: Then Narasambhaṭṭa, son of Subrahmanya, having been initiated by Gaṅgādhara got the appellation Brahmānandaghana held the preceptorship of the Pīṭha for twenty-eight years. This great preceptor merged in Bhagavan Īśvara as He was teaching the disciples the Brahmasūtra, bhāṣya etc. in the early morning of Aṣṭami of Kṛṣṇapakṣa in the month of Kārtika in the year Īśvara.

𑌸𑍁𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌭𑌵𑍋 𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑍍𑌯 𑌨𑌰𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌟𑍍𑌟𑍋𑌽𑌥 𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌧𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍

998aa3b8ab.b: Total lunar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈12.0 of 12 aṅgulas), Moon at the Rahu node (mukha/ascending).
998aa3b8ab.d: Umbral magnitude: 1.36 (parimāṇa ≈12.0 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 09:10►02:25 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra śatabhiṣak/pūrvaprōṣṭhapadā/uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or punarvasuḥ (anujanma) or viśākhā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: kumbhaḥ, mīnaḥ, karkaṭaḥ, vr̥śchikaḥ get more ashubha phala, mithunam, siṁhaḥ, tulā, makaraḥ somewhat ashubha, mēṣaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ, kanyā, dhanuḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
998aa3b8ab.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌮𑍀 𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌪𑌰𑌾।

9a2bffc224.d:
Perform Tarpana to Yamadharmaraja (even those with father). jīvatpitā'pi kurvīta tarpaṇaṁ yamabhīṣmayōḥ
एकैकेन तिलैर्मिश्रान् दद्यात् त्रींस्त्रीन् जलाञ्जलीन्।
संवत्सरकृतं पापं तत्क्षणादेव नश्यति॥
कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दश्यां यां काञ्चित् सरितं प्रति।
यमुनायां विशेषेण नियतस्तर्पयेद् यमम्॥
यत्र क्वचन नद्यां हि स्नात्वा कृष्णचतुर्दशीम्।
सन्तर्प्य धर्मराजं तु मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः॥
दक्षिणभिमुखो भूत्वा तिलैः सव्यं समाहितः।
देवतीर्थेन देवत्वात् तिलैः प्रेताधिपो यतः॥

१. यमं तर्पयामि। (त्रिः)
२. धर्मराजं तर्पयामि।
३. मृत्युं तर्पयामि।
४. अन्तकं तर्पयामि।
५. वैवस्वतं तर्पयामि।
६. कालं तर्पयामि।
७. सर्वभूतक्षयं तर्पयामि।
८. औदुम्बरं तर्पयामि।
९. दध्नं तर्पयामि।
१०. नीलं तर्पयामि।
११. परमेष्ठिनं तर्पयामि।
१२. वृकोदरं तर्पयामि।
१३. चित्रं तर्पयामि।
१४. चित्रगुप्तं तर्पयामि।


Perform Japa of the following names—
यमो निहन्ता पितृधर्मराजो वैवस्वतो दण्डधरश्च कालः।
प्रेताधिपो दत्तकृतानुसारी कृतान्तः (एतद् दशकृज्जपन्ति)॥

Perform namaskāraḥ—
नीलपर्वतसङ्काशो रुद्रकोपसमुद्भवः।
कालो दण्डधरो देवो वैवस्वत नमोऽस्तु ते॥

9ae59f93e6.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Trayōdaśī tithi of Bhādrapadaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti). The event occurred in 4141 (Kali era).
9ae59f93e6.d: Son of Śiva of Karnataka called Haripaṇḍita subsequently known by the name Śrī Pūrṇabodha (after initiation) held the preceptorship of the Pīṭha (Jagatgurupada) for twenty-six years. This realised preceptor merged in his illustrious effulgence in the early hours on the trayodaśī of Kṛṣṇapakṣa in the month Bhādrapada of the year Pramāthī.
9ae59f93e6.s:
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌟𑍋 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌪𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌿𑌤𑌃 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌸𑍁𑌤𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌬𑍋𑌧𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌯𑌾  
𑌬𑌿𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍋𑌽𑌨𑍁𑌪𑌦𑌂 𑌜𑌗𑌦𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌪𑌦𑌂 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌂𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌷𑌡𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍍।  
𑌧𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌨𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍇 𑌜𑌗𑌾𑌮 𑌨𑌿𑌲𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍇  
𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍌𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌪𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑌤𑌿𑌥𑍌 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌣𑍇 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍॥௮௭॥  
—𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌰𑍀

9aea3396b3.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Dvitīyā tithi of Āṣāḍhaḥ (lunar) month (Chandrōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
9aea3396b3.d: Bhagavan Mahavishnu sleeps with Devi Mahalakshmi on this day. Do Puja by placing Bhagavan/Devi on a new bed with pillow/blanket. Do danam of same after puja.
9aea3396b3.s:
𑌮𑌦𑌨𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌨𑍇 𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍇---  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣 𑌉𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌶𑍇𑌤𑍇 𑌜𑌗𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌾 𑌸𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌨𑍃𑌪।  
𑌅𑌶𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌶𑌯𑌨𑌾 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑌾 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌃॥  
𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤।  
(𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑍇 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑌃 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌃।)  
𑌵𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑍇𑌣 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣-𑌕𑌾𑌮-𑌯𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍋-𑌮𑌾𑌪𑌤𑌿-𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮-𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌪𑌮𑌭𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌯---  
𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌪𑌿𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌜𑌾𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌃।  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾 𑌸𑌾 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌸𑍁𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌶𑌯𑌨𑍋𑌚𑌿𑌤𑌾॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌾𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌚𑍍𑌯 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌂 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌜𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑌂 𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌗𑌨𑍍𑌧𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍁𑌨𑍇॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌯 𑌶𑌯𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌪𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍।  
𑌇𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌾 𑌆𑌷𑌾𑌢𑍍𑌯𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌵𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌭𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍।  
𑌇𑌮𑌮𑍁𑌚𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌰𑌯𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌮𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌜𑌗𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍍---  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌧𑌾𑌰𑌿 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌵𑌾𑌸 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌪𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌯।  
𑌗𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌾𑌶𑌂 𑌮𑍇 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍁 𑌧𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌕𑌾𑌮𑌦𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌶𑍁𑌚𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌰𑌾𑌃।  
𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌗𑌾 𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌭𑍇𑌦𑌤𑌃॥  
(𑌶𑍁𑌚𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌯𑌃। 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌰𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌃। 𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌗𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑌰𑌃।)  
𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑍇𑌵 𑌨 𑌕𑌦𑌾𑌚𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍।  
𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌕𑌲𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵 𑌮𑌾 𑌮𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌨 𑌶𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑌰𑌦 𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌤𑍇 𑌶𑌯𑌨𑌂 𑌸𑌦𑌾।  
𑌶𑌯𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌮𑌮𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌸𑍂𑌦𑌨।  
𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌰𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌤𑍁---  
𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌨𑍀 𑌭𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌂 𑌚 𑌭𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌮𑍍।  
𑌨𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌦𑍁𑌃𑌖𑌂 𑌦𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍁॥  
𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑍁𑌤𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌵 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑌥𑌾।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌵 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑍇𑌶 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌵𑌯𑍋𑌃॥  
𑌮𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌮 𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌾 𑌧𑌨𑌂 𑌮𑌾 𑌕𑍁𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌃।  
𑌅𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑌭𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌵𑌯𑍋𑌃॥ 𑌇𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌃।  
𑌏𑌵𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌹𑌰𑍇𑌃।  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌤𑌫𑌲𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌃।  
𑌅𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌃---  
𑌗𑌗𑌨𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌣𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍀𑌪 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍀𑌰𑌾𑌬𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌮𑌥𑌨𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌵।  
𑌭𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌦𑌿𑌗𑌾𑌭𑍋𑌗 𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌜 𑌨𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍇॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌤𑌨𑍇 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌂 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑍀𑌤 𑌵𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌃।  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌯 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌿 𑌶𑌯𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌯𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌦𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌣𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌬𑌾𑌹𑍋 𑌕𑌾𑌲𑍇 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌫𑌲𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚।  
𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌨 𑌤𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌨 𑌚𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌕𑌟𑍁𑌕𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚॥  
𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌨𑍃𑌪𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌠 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌶𑌯𑌨𑍇𑌽𑌨𑌘।  
𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌚 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌨𑍋𑌵𑌲𑍍𑌲𑌭𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌜𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌕𑌟𑍁𑌕𑌤𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌲𑌿𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌖𑌰𑍍𑌜𑍂𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍁𑌲𑌿𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌸𑌾 𑌸𑌹।  
(𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌸𑌾 𑌦𑍃𑌢𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍀𑌕𑍇𑌲𑌫𑌲𑍇𑌨𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌃।)  
𑌏𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌵 𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌗𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑍇𑌯 𑌸𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚॥  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑍇𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌚 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤।  
𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍋𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌏𑌵𑌂 𑌕𑌰𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌯𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌙𑍍𑌨𑌰𑍋 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑌭𑌙𑍍𑌗𑍋 𑌨 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑍇---  
𑌗𑍀𑌤𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍋𑌷𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌘𑌣𑍍𑌟𑌾 𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌯𑍀 𑌯𑌤𑌃॥  
𑌏𑌵𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌗𑍋𑌵𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌮𑌶𑍍𑌨𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍈𑌲𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌰𑌲𑌵𑌣𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌯𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌤𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌤𑍇 𑌸𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌾𑌤𑍇 𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍀𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌦𑍀𑌪𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌭𑍋𑌜𑌨𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑌯𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌚𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌣𑌃॥  
𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍁𑌕𑍋𑌪𑌾𑌨𑌹𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌚𑌾𑌮𑌰𑌾𑌸𑌨𑌸𑌂𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌅𑌭𑍀𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍋𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌰𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌰𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍃𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌸𑍋𑌪𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌕𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌧𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌭𑌰𑌣𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌯𑌥𑌾𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿-𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌅𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾 𑌗𑍌𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌯 𑌵𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌵𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑍁𑌟𑍁𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌿𑌨𑍇।  
𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍁𑌷𑍇 𑌨 𑌬𑌕𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌕𑍍𑌵𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌪𑌵𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌲𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌤𑌃।  
𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌭𑍋𑌜𑌨𑌂 𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌭𑍋𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌸𑍌𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑍀𑌮𑍁𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑍋𑌦𑌕𑍁𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌿𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌏𑌵𑌂 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌪𑍁𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌶𑌯𑌨𑌂 𑌹𑌰𑍇𑌃।  
𑌨 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌰𑌹𑌃 𑌕𑌦𑌾𑌚𑌿𑌦𑌪𑌿 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇।  
𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍀 𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌵𑌾 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌚𑍍𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌤𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌮𑍍। 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍇---  
𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌂 𑌨 𑌶𑍋𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌦𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌕𑍍𑌵𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍।  
𑌨 𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌶𑍁𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮॥  
𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌶𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚।  
𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌶𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌶𑌯𑌨𑌂 𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌲𑍋𑌕𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑍀𑌯𑌤𑍇॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌦𑌯𑍇 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌦𑌯𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌵 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾। 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍋𑌃 𑌪𑌰𑍈𑌵।  
𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌵𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁।  
𑌅𑌶𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌜𑌯𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌫𑌲𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌕𑌮𑍍। 𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑌚𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍।

9b128e94b0.d: Guruḥ rises out of combustion (udayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2025-Jul-08 14:38. At this moment guruḥ is at ārdrā-2 mithunam (latitude 0°07′04.02″ S, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -1.89, elongation 9°58′46.72″ W of the Sun. Emergence from combustion restores a graha's full strength; this is generally considered an auspicious time to begin activities connected with guruḥ's significations.

9b3f156d6d.d:
When Pushya nakshatra falls on a Thursday, it is a special yōgaḥ. In the cyclic rotation of time, along with the bad combinations of grahas and nakshatras that indicate the probability of upcoming difficulties, good combinations that grant benefits in multiples also arise. Among such good combinations are the Amrita Siddhi yogas of certain weekdays and nakshatras. They are Sunday-Hasta, Monday-Mrigashirsha, Tuesday-Ashvini, Wednesday-Anuradha, Thursday-Pushya, Friday-Revati, Saturday-Rohini. Good deeds performed on such yogas become especially strong in protecting and nourishing us.
For instance, in Devi Atharvashirsha, it is said bhaumāśvinyāṁ mahādevī-sannidhau japtvā mahāmr̥tyuṁ tarati, that is, one can cross even mahāmr̥tyu by doing parayanam when Tuesday and Ashvini join.
9b3f156d6d.s:
𑌆𑌦𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌯𑍋𑌗𑍇 𑌬𑍁𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌧𑌾 𑌶𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍋𑌹𑌿𑌣𑍀 𑌚।  
𑌸𑍋𑌮𑍇 𑌚 𑌸𑍌𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌭𑍃𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍇𑌵𑌤𑍀 𑌚 𑌭𑍌𑌮𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌨𑍀 𑌚𑌾𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌃॥

9bbde49f96.d: Guruḥ sets into combustion (astamayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2026-Jul-16 14:54. At this moment guruḥ is at puṣyaḥ-2 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 0°27′22.68″ N, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -1.79, elongation 9°38′23.93″ E of the Sun. Combustion (mAudhyam) is generally considered to weaken a graha's ability to give full results in its significations; undertakings connected with guruḥ are traditionally best avoided until it re-emerges.

9bfb89b055.b: Observed on Śukla-Daśamī tithi of Pauṣaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
9bfb89b055.d:
Sāmba, the son of Sri Krishna, was cured of leprosy after performing tapaḥ to propitiate Surya Bhagavan. sāmba was the son of Bhagavan Sri Krishna and Jambavan's daughter, Jambavati. He was afflicted with leprosy owing to some sins accumulated in previous births. Deeply remorseful, he approached his father, Sri Krishna. Bhagavan pointed out that there was no other recourse to curing this disease other than the upāsana of sūrya bhagavān and narrated the method to propitiate Surya Bhagavan and the story of a chaṇḍāla strī who had gotten cured from disease by Surya Bhagavan. sāmba then propitiated Surya Bhagavan with bhakti. Pleased with his devotion, Surya Bhagavan revealed to him the āryādvādaśakam stuti (http://stotrasamhita.net/wiki/Dwadasharya_Surya_Stuti). Performing pārāyaṇam of this stuti, sambā was cured of this debilitating disease.

ஜகத்குருவான பகவான் ஶ்ரீக்ருஷணருக்கும் ஜாம்பவானது புத்ரியான ஜாம்பவதிக்கும் பிறந்தவர் ஸாம்பன்.  அவருக்கு ஜன்மாந்தரத்தில் செய்த பாபத்தால் குஷ்டரோகம் பாதித்தது. அதனால் மிகவும் வருந்திய அவர் தந்தையான ஶ்ரீக்ருஷ்ணரையே ஶரணடைந்தார். பகவானும் ஸூர்ய-உபாஸனையைத் தவிர இதற்கு வேறு உபாயமில்லை என்று கூறி ஸூர்யனை உபாஸிக்கும் முறைகளை உபதேஶித்து ஸூர்யபகவானால் நோயிலிருந்து குணமடைந்த சண்டாள ஸ்த்ரீயின் வ்ருத்தாந்தத்தையும் கூறினார். பிறகு ஸாம்பன் பக்தியுடன் ஸூர்யபகாவானை உபாஸித்தார். இதனால் மகிழ்ந்த ஸூர்ய பகவான் ஸாம்பனுக்கு “ஆர்யாத்வாதஶகம்” (http://stotrasamhita.net/wiki/Dwadasharya_Surya_Stuti) என்ற இந்த ஸ்துதியை அருளினார். அதை பாராயணம் செய்து மஹாரோகமான குஷ்டரோகத்திலிருந்து குணமடைந்தார்.

9c16361bef.b: Observed on Śukla-Dvādaśī tithi of Kārttikaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti).
9c16361bef.s:
𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌅𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌧𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌰𑍇𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌲𑌯𑌃॥  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌗𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌗𑌜𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌾𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃---  
𑌆𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌛𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍀 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾।  
𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾 𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌭𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌦𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚॥  
𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾।  
𑌆𑌷𑌾𑌢𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌦𑌶𑌮𑍀 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍀॥  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌷𑌾𑌢𑍀 𑌚 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾।  
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑍀 𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀 𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾॥  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌾𑌃।  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁॥  
𑌹𑌾𑌯𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌦𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌆𑌸𑍁 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌜𑌪𑍋 𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---   
𑌯𑌾 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃।  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌤𑌦𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑌲𑌿𑌲𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌲𑌿𑌃।  
𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌹𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌬𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌯𑌥𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿।  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌜𑌪𑍋 𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌪𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌷𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌚𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌮𑌣𑍌 𑌮𑌨𑍁𑌃---  
𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁।  
𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁॥

9c36d29c71.b: Observed on Ārdrā nakshatra of Karkaṭaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
9c36d29c71.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

This Nayanmar, a chieftain from Kalandai, was a fervent devotee of Bhagavan Shiva. His daily spiritual practices included the repetition of the Panchakshara Mantra and the service of Shiva Bhaktas. Recognizing his devotion, Bhagavan Shiva blessed him with increased power, wealth, and strength. The Nayanmar's influence grew to such an extent that he conquered many regions within the Chola and Pandyan kingdoms. He expressed a desire to be crowned king by the three thousand Brahmanas of Tillai, but they declined, owing their allegiance to the Chola king. This led to the Brahmanas leaving Tillai to avoid the Nayanmar's anger, leaving only one to perform Puja in the temple. Even this lone Brahmana refused to crown him. In response to his prayers, Bhagavan Shiva personally appeared and crowned the Nayanmar, placing His divine Feet upon his head, symbolizing a spiritual coronation. The Nayanmar continued his devout worship of Bhagavan Shiva and ultimately achieved union with Him, demonstrating that his request for coronation was not for political power, but for spiritual affirmation and blessings from Bhagavan.
9c36d29c71.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society

9cdee22701.b: Observed on Svātī nakshatra of Mithunam (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).

9d24363b72.d: The three days around the Ashtaka Shraaddha of  mārgaśīrṣa, pauṣa and māgha month are anadhyayana days, where one is not supposed to learn the Vedas.
9d24363b72.s:
𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌪𑍌𑌷𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵 𑌚॥௭௬॥  
𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌾𑌃 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌸𑍂𑌰𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌃।  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌕𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌷𑌟𑍍‌𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍇 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑍇

9d3fa0e00b.d: Aṣṭamī tithi on a Wednesday is as sacred as a solar eclipse. When śuklāṣṭamī tithi falls on a Wednesday in puṣyamāsa, it is even more sacred, and known by the name mahābhadrā.
9d3fa0e00b.s:
𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌿 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌬𑍁𑌧𑍋 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑌾 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌭𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌤𑌿 𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌾॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌜𑌪𑍋 𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍍𑌪𑌣𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑍋𑌜𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌤𑌯𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌿 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌹𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌬𑍁𑌧𑍈𑌃॥  
(𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿-𑌕𑍌𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌭𑍇)  
  
𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌤𑌯𑍇 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌿 𑌶𑌤𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌦𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌿 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌹𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌰𑍈𑌃॥  
(𑌪𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌷𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌚𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌮𑌣𑍌)  
  
𑌅𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑍋𑌮𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍀 𑌭𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌨𑌾 𑌸𑌹।  
𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀 𑌭𑍂𑌮𑌿𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌣 𑌸𑍋𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌣 𑌚𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀।  
𑌚𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌤𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌣𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌭𑌾𑌃॥  
(𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌫𑌲𑍇)

9dd8c1a543.b: Observed on Paurṇamāsī tithi of Jyaiṣṭhaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti).
9dd8c1a543.s:
𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌅𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌧𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌰𑍇𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌲𑌯𑌃॥  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌗𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌗𑌜𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌾𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃---  
𑌆𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌛𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍀 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾।  
𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾 𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌭𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌦𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚॥  
𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾।  
𑌆𑌷𑌾𑌢𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌦𑌶𑌮𑍀 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍀॥  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌷𑌾𑌢𑍀 𑌚 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾।  
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑍀 𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀 𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾॥  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌾𑌃।  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁॥  
𑌹𑌾𑌯𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌦𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌆𑌸𑍁 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌜𑌪𑍋 𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---   
𑌯𑌾 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃।  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌤𑌦𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑌲𑌿𑌲𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌲𑌿𑌃।  
𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌹𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌬𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌯𑌥𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿।  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌜𑌪𑍋 𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌪𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌷𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌚𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌮𑌣𑍌 𑌮𑌨𑍁𑌃---  
𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁।  
𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁॥

9e53be53f4.d: ಕುಮಾರವ್ಯಾಸ ಕಾವ್ಯನಾಮದಿಂದ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧನಾಗಿರುವ ಗದುಗಿನ ನಾರಣಪ್ಪನು ಸಮೀಪದ ಕೋಳಿವಾಡದವನಾದರೂ ಅವನ ಕಾವ್ಯ ಪ್ರತಿಭೆ ಬೆಳಗಿದ್ದು ಗದಗಿನ ವೀರನಾರಯಣ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನದಲ್ಲಿ. ಗದುಗಿನ ಭಾರತ, ಕರ್ಣಾಟ ಭಾರತ ಕಥಾಮಂಜರಿ, ಕುಮಾರವ್ಯಾಸ ಭಾರತ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಹೆಸರುಗಳಿಂದ ಕರೆಯಲ್ಪಡುವ ಅಪೂರ್ವ ಗ್ರಂಥವನ್ನು ರಚಿಸಿದ ಕುಮಾರವ್ಯಾಸ ಕೊನೇರಿ ತೀರ್ಥದ ಜಲದಲ್ಲಿ ನಿತ್ಯ ಮಿಂದು ವೀರನಾರಯಣ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನದ ರಂಗ ಮಂಟಪದ ಎರಡನೇ ಕಂಬದ ಹತ್ತಿರ ಶ್ರೀ ವೀರನಾರಯಣನ ಸಮ್ಮುಖದಲ್ಲಿ ಒದ್ದೆ ಬಟ್ಟೆ ಉಟ್ಟು ಬರೆಯಲು ಕುಳಿತರೆ ಶ್ರೀ ವೀರನಾರಯಣನೇ ಕವಿಯಾಗಿ, ಕುಮಾರವ್ಯಾಸ ಲಿಪಿಕಾರನಾಗಿ ಪಂಚಮವೇದವು ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಕಥೆಯಾಗಿ ಬರುತ್ತದೆ.

𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇 𑌵𑌨𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌣𑌿 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌶𑌤𑌤𑌮𑍇𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑍇  
𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌯𑌸𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍌—  
𑌆𑌷𑌾𑌢𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌮𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌗𑌯𑌾 𑌮𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌾।  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌗𑌜𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌾𑌯𑌾 𑌗𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍁𑌲𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌪𑍈𑌤𑍃𑌕𑍇॥
